messages:
alex: quick idea — can we explore a compact delta encoding for the model rollout surface? thinking about reducing webhook/poll payload sizes for tenants that have lots of pins :thinking_face:
maya: curious, do you mean a binary diff or a folded key-delta in the json?
alex: folded key-delta in JSON (or base64 protobuf as an option). avoid full manifest roundtrips when only leases/weights change. payloads often >50KB for large variant lists.
sam: +1 to smaller payloads. but big gotcha: clients need deterministic replay semantics. if we send delta x->y, what if client missed x? we need a gap-resilient resolver.
nina: exactly. either require clients to fetch full snapshot periodically (every N deltas) or include a compact anchor version in every delta.
alex: proposal sketch: every delta carries: base_version (string), target_version, ops[] where ops = [path, op_type, value?], and optional full_snapshot boolean when we force snapshot. small and composable.
maya: how about encoding ops as short tokens to save bytes, eg 's' for set, 'r' for remove, 'i' for increment? still JSON but small keys.
sam: okay but then we add decoding burden on language SDKs. we need SDK helpers in platform libs that hide the tokens. DevEx work.
nina: telemetry question: how do we measure delta application failures? we should tag delta messages with delta_id + origin so ops-failures show up in rollout telemetry and we can correlate with API errors.
alex: yes include delta_id and checksum (sha256) so client can verify. if checksum mismatch, client triggers full snapshot fetch.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-metadata-service v2.3 -> staging (tag: compact-delta-experiment) :rocket:
maya: compatibility: older clients that don't understand deltas should ignore unknown fields and fall back to full snapshot polling. but we must ensure safe defaults server-side: always send full snapshot as fallback if client version < X.
sam: tradeoff: server needs to maintain both delta and snapshot generation. space/time cost on control plane. but we can lazily materialize deltas per tenant using change logs.
alex: what about TTL/expiry semantics? if delta just includes 'lease_ttl' adjustments, clients must ensure they don't extend or shorten incorrectly. maybe deltas only express relative operations (e.g., +3600) vs absolute to avoid clock skew issues.
nina: relative ops avoid timezone/clock edgecases. but absolute timestamps make auditing simpler. propose: deltas carry both when available: op_relative and op_absolute optional; client applies absolute when present and validates with checksum.
maya: don't forget offline reconcilation for on-prem/private deployments — binary/protobuf deltas might be preferable there (smaller, faster), but for hosted API JSON is more transparent for logs and debugging.
sam: then we should support two encodings behind the same delta envelope: content_type: application/json-delta or application/proto-delta; clients negotiate via Accept-Delta header.
alex: rollout plan: 1) implement delta generator + anchor-versioning on control plane (no client changes), 2) ship SDK helpers and server Accept-Delta negotiation, 3) opt-in tenant experiments, 4) monitor telemetry and error-rate before defaulting to deltas.
nina: migration window idea: 2 weeks opt-in + 1 week canary auto-fallback. also telemetry gates: if delta_applied_failure_rate > 0.5% revert for that tenant.
maya: ops concern: need a replay tool to rehydrate client state given a sequence of deltas + snapshot. add a small CLI: `redwood-rollout replay --from=V1 --to=V5 --apply` to help debug.
sam: security: sign deltas with control-plane key. clients verify signature locally. avoids malicious/man-in-the-middle tamper.
alex: good point. add sig + key_id in envelope. key rotation story: include keyset endpoint and key_id in delta metadata.
nina: thoughts on observability naming? suggest metric names: rollout.delta.sent, rollout.delta.applied, rollout.delta.failed, rollout.delta.checksum_mismatch. sample tags: tenant_id, delta_id, base_version.
maya: and traces: add a span for delta_verification and delta_application in client SDKs for smoother triage.
alex: any objections to short token ops in JSON (maya's idea) + protobuf option?
sam: no objections, just backlog for SDKs. add explicit feature-flag header so we can turn on/off per-tenant.
nina: last q: should deltas be order-preserving? i.e., server guarantees monotonic delta sequence numbers per tenant. I think yes, otherwise clients cannot apply them safely.
alex: agreed — monotonic sequence numbers are required. include seq_num in every delta.
maya: i'll write a short RFC note with examples and a minimal compatibility matrix. alex, can you put the sketch ops list in the RFC?
alex: on it. will paste example: ```json
{
  "base_version":"v12",
  "target_version":"v13",
  "seq_num": 45,
  "delta_id":"d_20260321_01",
  "ops":[["variants.2.weight","s",0.1],["leases.tenant123","r"]],
  "checksum":"abc123...",
  "content_type":"application/json-delta"
}
```
sam: love the example. nina: i'll add telemetry and failure gates to the RFC.
alex: cool. if no objections we'll spin up an experiment in staging next week. :thumbsup:
maya: SGTM.
nina: SGTM.
sam: SGTM.
deploy-bot: staging rollout started for experiment group: 12 tenants.
